title: Slow conversion when loading from CSV and saving as Parquet
body: I am loading several large datasets containing 20GB or more of CSV data and exporting them to Parquet for subsequent processing. With DuckDB 0.7.1, loading a gzip-compressed CSV into a local on-disk database takes about three minutes, but copying the table to Parquet takes upwards of three hours. I use all_varchar=true because of the source data. This is on an Apple Silicon M1 iMac with 16GB RAM, a 1TB SSD, and macOS Ventura 13.2.1. Is there a faster way to perform this conversion?

symptoms_visible: With DuckDB 0.7.1, loading my gzip-compressed CSV into a local table takes about three minutes, but writing that table to Parquet takes upwards of three hours.
N0.label: N0 very slow Parquet export reported

symptoms_visible: On v0.7.2-dev1322, a direct gzip-CSV-to-ZSTD-Parquet conversion completes in about 550 seconds instead of taking three hours.
The direct conversion takes about the same time with preserve_insertion_order set to either true or false.
N1.label: N1 latest development build greatly improves baseline

symptoms_visible: With experimental_parallel_csv enabled, the direct conversion finishes in 31.687 seconds, but the resulting Parquet file contains only 30,559,373 rows.
Reading the same gzip CSV without the experimental parallel reader returns 212,363,079 rows.
N2.label: N2 experimental parallel gzip read loses rows

symptoms_visible: The uncompressed CSV converts with the parallel reader and produces all 212,363,079 rows.

In my benchmark matrix, every gzip-compressed input processed with experimental_parallel_csv produces an unusually small Parquet file, while the corresponding serial runs produce multi-gigabyte files.
N3.label: N3 compressed-input defect isolated by controls

symptoms_visible: After updating to a build containing PR 6977, the conversion commands complete, but read_parquet fails with 'No magic bytes found at end of file'.
N4_x.label: N4_x PR 6977 alone leaves unreadable Parquet output

symptoms_visible: With v0.7.2-dev2675, the compressed CSV converts to Parquet in about 2 minutes 57 seconds, and read_parquet successfully reports all 212,363,079 rows.
N_terminal.label: terminal fast and correct one-pass conversion

question_patterns: Can you retry the conversion with the latest master build and report the timing?
Please test a current development build, since a recent VARCHAR-to-Parquet performance issue was fixed.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested v0.7.2-dev1322. A direct COPY from ccaed182.csv.gz to ZSTD Parquet took 549.536 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest master still takes about three hours for the same conversion.
The same development build completes in about ten minutes rather than 549.536 seconds.

question_patterns: What happens if you set preserve_insertion_order=false before writing Parquet?
Can you compare the direct conversion with and without insertion-order preservation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The direct gzip conversion took 549.536 seconds normally and 551.849 seconds with preserve_insertion_order=false. Both output files were 4,794,409,184 bytes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Setting preserve_insertion_order=false reduces the same serial gzip conversion from about nine minutes to under one minute.

solution.intent: Move off DuckDB 0.7.1 to a current development build containing the recent VARCHAR Parquet writer performance fix, and allow unordered Parquet writes when row order is not required.
solution.concrete_example: Retry on the latest master because the VARCHAR-column Parquet performance problem was recently fixed in #6852. If output row order is not required, run SET preserve_insertion_order=false before COPY so the Parquet writer can use parallelism.
solution.inference_hint: The connection between the 0.7.1 behavior and the recently fixed VARCHAR Parquet writer issue comes from the maintainer. The reporter supplies only the workload and measured timings.

edges.comment: The reporter installed and retained v0.7.2-dev1322, so the system state changes. The direct conversion drops from roughly three hours to roughly nine minutes, while preserve_insertion_order=false alone cannot parallelize a serial gzip CSV source.

question_patterns: Can you run COPY over a SELECT from read_csv_auto so all_varchar can be supplied without creating an intermediate table?
Please try COPY (SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(..., all_varchar=true)) TO ... and report what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My first attempt to put read_csv_auto directly after COPY produced a parser error (I've attached my annotated screenshot of the COPY syntax diagram asking where all_varchar goes). Using COPY (select * from read_csv_auto('ccaed182.csv.gz', all_varchar=true)) TO ... worked.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The select-node form works after changing all_varchar=1 to all_varchar=true.

question_patterns: Can you enable experimental_parallel_csv, run the direct conversion, and check the resulting row count?
Please test the parallel CSV reader against the gzip input and report both elapsed time and count(*).
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With preserve_insertion_order=false and experimental_parallel_csv=true, the direct conversion finished in 31.687 seconds, but count(*) on the Parquet output was only 30,559,373.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The parallel run finishes quickly and the output contains the full 212,363,079 rows.
The parallel run takes 35 seconds and produces about 30.5 million rows.

question_patterns: What row count do you get from the same gzip file with the experimental parallel reader disabled?
Can you compare count(*) with experimental_parallel_csv set to false?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With experimental_parallel_csv=false, reading the same gzip file returned 212,363,079 rows and took 254.119 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The serial reader also returns only 30,559,373 rows.

edges.comment: The handler-initiated configuration tests are measurements even though the toggles could act as performance workarounds. The reporter gives only commands, timings, and row counts; the conclusion that the experimental gzip path drops data is not placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Does the parallel reader return the full row count when the same CSV is uncompressed?
Can you repeat the conversion against the decompressed CSV as a control?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the uncompressed ccaed182.csv, preserve_insertion_order=false and experimental_parallel_csv=true, COPY completed in 168.212 seconds. The Parquet output contains all 212,363,079 rows.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The uncompressed control also produces only about 30 million rows.
The uncompressed control takes about three minutes and still contains all 212,363,079 rows.

question_patterns: Can you benchmark the combinations of compressed versus uncompressed input, direct versus select-node COPY, insertion-order preservation, and parallel CSV reading?
Please compare output sizes and timings across those reader and writer settings.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran all 16 combinations. The gzip inputs with experimental_parallel_csv=true produced files around 588MB to 681MB, while the corresponding complete outputs were roughly 4.14GB to 4.82GB. The attached table contains the timings and sizes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All 16 combinations produce the same row count and approximately the same output size.
The same compressed parallel cases are abnormally small, with minor timing differences between runs.

edges.comment: The uncompressed control and the 16-case benchmark isolate the bad observation to compressed input combined with the experimental parallel reader. The reporter does not identify the implementation defect.

solution.intent: Update to the build containing PR 6977, which replaces the experimental parallel CSV path and fixes the compressed-input row-loss behavior.
solution.concrete_example: Build current master after PR 6977 and rerun the compressed CSV conversion using the parallel CSV reader, then validate the generated Parquet files.
solution.inference_hint: The raw controls show that only compressed parallel reads lose rows. Mapping that behavior to the gzip handling fixed by the parallel CSV reader work is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: PR 6977 fixes the earlier compressed parallel-reader row loss, but this attempt is insufficient for the reporter's large 16GB-RAM workload: COPY appears to finish while the resulting Parquet files have no valid footer. Because the reporter compiled and retained the new version, this reaches system state S3.

solution.intent: Update to a current build containing both the corrected parallel CSV reader and the memory-usage fix from #7253, perform the gzip CSV to Parquet conversion in one pass, and verify the resulting Parquet row count before declaring success.
solution.concrete_example: Compile or install a current DuckDB build containing the parallel CSV reader corrections and #7253, then run COPY (SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('ccaed182.csv.gz', all_varchar=true)) TO 'ccaed182.parquet' (FORMAT PARQUET, CODEC ZSTD), using preserve_insertion_order=false if row order is unnecessary. Please retest in the current build and confirm that read_parquet can open the file and count all expected rows.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter observes that PR 6977 outputs cannot be opened because they lack terminal magic bytes. The maintainer identifies high memory usage and the OOM killer as the cause and fixes it in #7253; that diagnosis must not be attributed to the reporter.

edges.comment: The reporter compiled v0.7.2-dev2675 after #7253, retained it as system state S4, and verified a readable full-row-count Parquet file in 177 seconds. The verification result is terminal-side and is not required information for proposing the fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original performance problem as the combination of DuckDB 0.7.1's VARCHAR-to-Parquet performance issue and serialization constraints; a current build plus unordered writes when order is unnecessary enables the fast path.

Must ground the compressed-input diagnosis in the measured counts and controls: the experimental parallel gzip path produced 30,559,373 rows versus 212,363,079 serially, while parallel reading of the uncompressed CSV returned the full count.
Must not recommend experimental_parallel_csv on the old development build as a valid solution, because its apparently fast gzip conversion produced incomplete output.
Must not treat PR 6977 alone as sufficient for this workload: the generated files could not be read and reported 'No magic bytes found at end of file'.
The complete fix must include the corrected parallel CSV reader and the #7253 high-memory/OOM fix, while preserving all_varchar handling through a SELECT over read_csv_auto.
Must ask the reporter to verify both Parquet readability and the expected 212,363,079-row count on a build containing the fixes before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical independent developer who is comfortable compiling DuckDB from source, writing SQL and Ruby benchmark scripts, comparing configuration matrices, inspecting file sizes, and validating output row counts.
persona_hint.communication_style: Enthusiastic, collaborative, and evidence-heavy; reports exact commands, versions, timings, counts, and file sizes, and proactively runs broad benchmark matrices when behavior is inconsistent.
